memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"In days to come, when your son asks you, 'What does this mean?' say to him,
'With a mighty hand the LORD brought us out of Egypt, out of the land of
slavery.'" - Ex 13:14 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
This is the second time in one chapter that God anticipates a child's question.
He clearly expects the practices of faith to raise questions in young minds.

Notice again what the answer is. Not a defence of the ritual, not an explanation
of religious procedure. A story about rescue. "The LORD brought us out."

There is wisdom in this for anyone raising children or mentoring younger
believers. When a child asks why we pray before eating, or why we go to church,
or why we give, the temptation is to answer with rules. "Because that is what we
do." That answer closes the door. The better answer opens it: "Because of what
God has done for us."

Rules without story produce religion. Story produces faith.

Notice too that God does not treat the child's question as a nuisance or a sign
of rebellion. He plans for it. Honest questions are welcome in the household of
faith. A child who asks is a child who is engaging.

If your children or grandchildren are asking hard questions, that is not a
crisis. It may be an invitation.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. When someone asks you why, do you answer with rules or with what God has
   done?
2. Is your home a place where questions are welcome?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, help me to welcome questions rather than fear them, and to answer with
the story of Your goodness. Amen.
